record.question:
A company runs a provisioned Amazon Redshift cluster. Its disaster recovery objectives for a Region outage are a recovery point objective (RPO) of 24 hours and a recovery time objective (RTO) of 1 hour. Repeated recovery exercises have restored a representative snapshot in the recovery Region and completed client cutover within 40 minutes. The company wants to avoid paying for an always-running recovery cluster.

Which configuration best supports these objectives?

options.text: Take automated snapshots in the primary Region. Start copying the latest snapshot to the recovery Region only after a Region outage is declared.

Enable automated snapshots and cross-Region snapshot copying. Monitor that the latest successfully copied recovery point is less than 24 hours old, and maintain the tested restore-and-cutover runbook and recovery dependencies.
Enable cross-Region synchronous replication between the Redshift cluster and a continuously running standby cluster, then configure automatic DNS failover.
Rely on the default automated snapshots in the primary Region. During an outage, restore those snapshots to a different Availability Zone in that same Region.

explanation.text:
<<2>> places recoverable data outside the failure Region before the incident. Snapshot copy produces backups, not a running cluster. On failure, restore from the destination copy and execute the tested client cutover.

<<1>> depends on an unavailable source Region during the incident. <<3>> describes neither the snapshot-copy feature nor the requested cost model, and Redshift does not provide the claimed synchronous cross-Region standby switch. <<4>> changes Availability Zone within the failed Region and provides no independently stored regional recovery copy.

RPO measures the age of the recoverable data; RTO measures the time to restore service. A schedule alone does not establish either result: monitor completed copies and rehearse restoration, permissions, capacity, networking, and cutover. The one-hour RTO is supported here by scenario-specific tests, not a service guarantee.

AWS documentation (checked 2026-09-18):
https://docs.aws.amazon.com/redshift/latest/mgmt/cross-region-snapshot-copy.html
https://docs.aws.amazon.com/redshift/latest/mgmt/working-with-snapshots.html

diagram_alt: The age of the copied snapshot and the duration of the recovery process are independent time budgets.

sources.supports: Automatic snapshot copying to another Region and destination restoration.
Snapshots are point-in-time backups; restoration creates a new cluster.

editorial_notes: Added observed restore evidence to make the 1-hour RTO defensible. Clarified that copying replicates snapshots, not an active cluster. Answer ID unchanged.
